options: An attacker pretends to be a trusted source to trick people into giving up information or access
Malware that spreads between computers without any user action
Software that guesses passwords at high speed
Flooding a website with traffic until it stops responding
explanation: Phishing relies on deception. The attacker impersonates someone trusted and persuades a person to act.

prompt: A text message says your parcel is on hold and asks you to pay a small fee through a link. What is this attack called?
options: Vishing
Smishing
Whaling
Pharming
explanation: Smishing is phishing delivered by SMS or chat apps. Vishing uses phone calls, and whaling targets senior leaders.

prompt: What makes spear phishing different from ordinary email phishing?
options: It is aimed at a specific person and uses personal details
It is only ever sent by phone
It always contains an attachment
It only targets company executives
explanation: Spear phishing is tailored to one target. Targeting executives specifically is called whaling.

prompt: A caller says they are from your bank's fraud team and asks you to read out the code that was just sent to your phone. What should you do?
options: Read the code, because they already know your name
Hang up and call the number printed on your bank card
Ask them to prove who they are and carry on with the call
Read out only the first three digits
explanation: Never trust a caller who contacted you. End the call and phone the bank using a number you already know. One-time codes must never be shared.

prompt: A finance manager gets an email addressed to them by name. It mentions a real supplier and asks them to update the supplier's bank details. Which type of attack is this most likely to be?
options: Mass email phishing
Spear phishing
Smishing
Quishing
explanation: The use of a real name, role and supplier shows the attacker researched the target. That is the mark of spear phishing.

prompt: A sticker on a parking meter shows a QR code to pay for parking. The page it opens asks for your full card details. What is this?
options: Quishing
Whaling
Vishing
Spear phishing
explanation: Quishing hides a malicious address inside a QR code. Use the operator's official app or website instead of scanning unknown codes.

prompt: Why do attackers favour phishing over attacking networks directly?
options: It targets people, so it can bypass firewalls and other technical controls
It needs expensive equipment that others cannot detect
It only works against old software
It cannot be traced by anyone
explanation: Phishing is cheap, scales to thousands of targets, and succeeds when a person makes a choice that no technical control can block.
